title: When irrelevance governs: dissipation-regression scaling in open quantum criticality
abstract: The real-time dynamics of quantum phase transitions in open systems coupled to finite-temperature environments sits at the heart of contemporary condensed-matter and quantum-information science. Here, invoking a Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we uncover that, within the coherence-dominated regime of critical real-time evolution, a dissipative coupling deemed naively irrelevant determines, counterintuitively, the longest timescale that holds sway. Possessing a well-defined temporal scaling dimension, it engenders a novel dissipation-regression scaling that systematically reproduces the unusual Kibble-Zurek scaling and relaxation observed in recent numerical studies. By contrast, dissipation-dominated dynamics behaves qualitatively differently. There, furthermore, we show that the discretized and diagonalized formulations of the same open quantum Ising chain realize distinct universality classes.
summary: This paper develops the Dissipation-Regression Scaling (DRS) framework to describe the real-time dynamics of quantum phase transitions in open quantum systems. Using advanced field theory techniques, the authors show that even couplings initially deemed irrelevant can dictate the system's longest timescale. This provides a unified explanation for unusual scaling behaviors observed in quantum criticality experiments and simulations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the real-time dynamics of quantum phase transitions in open quantum systems coupled to finite-temperature environments.
main_result: It introduces Dissipation-Regression Scaling (DRS), a novel scaling law that counterintuitively shows that a naively irrelevant dissipative coupling determines the longest timescale in the coherence-dominated regime.
method: The analysis employs the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism and Renormalization-Group (RG) theory, extending standard scaling hypotheses to account for dissipation effects.
model_or_system: The study focuses on open quantum systems, exemplified by the open quantum Ising chain, whose dynamics are governed by the Lindblad equation and analyzed using a bosonic quantum field theory approach.
key_observables: Excitation density (D) and topological defect density (related to Kibble-Zurek scaling).
important_parameters: Bath spectral exponent (s), coupling strength ($\lambda$), temperature (T), and the dynamic critical exponent (z).
main_assumptions: The theory distinguishes between coherence-dominated and dissipation-dominated regimes, and it notes that standard perturbation theory and simple scaling arguments are insufficient.
figures_summary: Not specified (The notes detail scaling equations and functional forms rather than describing figure content).
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general problem of QPT dynamics in open systems, develops the Schwinger-Keldysh framework, derives scaling forms for different regimes (quasi-equilibrium vs. FTS), and culminates in the proposal and validation of the DRS mechanism.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized scaling framework for non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding decoherence and relaxation in realistic quantum devices.
